Join us and shape the future of hospitality today!
Associate Dean – Degree Programs
Join us and shape the future of hospitality today!
EHL's dynamic campuses form a unique network where passionate students, academics and industry experts from over 120 countries come together with a common goal: to develop and disseminate hospitality knowledge, while supporting the sector's continued growth.
We are constantly striving to improve the working environment and personal development opportunities for our more than 800 staff and teachers, who are among the most recognized experts in their respective fields.

Since its foundation in 1893, EHL has been widely recognized by the industry and consistently ranked among the world's top hospitality management schools. Everything we do is based on our values of excellence, family and learning, and we are committed to bringing them to life in tangible ways for our employees.
The Hospitality Business School (HBS) at EHL is at the heart of EHL’s academic mission, shaping the future of hospitality, service, and human\-centric management. It designs and delivers high\-quality academic programs that combine academic rigor (AACSB, EFMD, NECHE) with strong industry relevance.

Working in close collaboration with faculty, industry partners, and support teams, HBS offers an inspiring and international learning environment. Driven by EHL’s values of excellence, learning, and care, HBS is committed to developing future\-ready leaders with a global mind\-set.
To join our amazing team, we are looking for a candidate who is not only skilled and passionate about hospitality but also aligns with our leadership principles: transparency, accountability, collaboration, care, and experimentation.
Associate Dean – Degree Programs
The Associate Dean – Degree Programs plays a key leadership role in strategic development, continuous improvement of degree programs (MSc, MBA, EMBA, DBA). The position ensures academic excellence, fosters innovation in teaching and learning. Moreover, they should demonstrate strong leadership skills, embodying our EHL leadership principles, and demonstrate excellent people skills to foster and nurture collaboration amongst our faculty members, the industry and our educational partners.
What will you do?
Define and implement the strategic vision for Master programs, ensuring alignment with institutional goals and evolving market trends.
Lead the development, design, assessment, and continuous improvement of degree program curricula.
Ensure overall program coherence and quality, including alignment of GLOs across courses, semesters, and the full program structure.
Maintain national and international academic standards in line with accreditation requirements and institutional objectives.
Foster collaboration across communities of practice and actively contribute to the Academic Board.
Coordinate with multiple departments and stakeholders to effectively resolve complex cross\-functional issues.

You have a PhD degree in business administration or hospitality management.
You have at least 10 years of experience in higher education, including profound teaching experience for graduate and post\-graduate programs.
You have proven managerial and administrative experience, have a track record of leading teams, and can implement policies and decisions effectively.
You are highly organized, with strong prioritization and problem\-solving skills, and the ability to analyze data from both strategic and detailed perspectives.
You have a solid scholarly publication record in terms of peer\-reviewed journal articles.
You are collaborative, with a proven ability to work effectively with faculty, administrators, staff, and students.
You have excellent verbal and written communication skills, along with strong interpersonal abilities.
You are fluent in English and French (C1\), German and/or Italian a plus.

We offer you a permanent contract within a business area of an educational institution, with exceptional employee benefits including free meals, an attractive number of days off, a parking space or public transport contribution, as well as access to various services and facilities.
We offer you responsibility, challenge, development opportunities and encouragement to help you achieve your professional and personal goals. In addition, we offer you the opportunity to make a tangible impact on our students’, staff and partners’ experience as well as contribute to the growth of our institution.
You will enjoy being part of a passionate, multidisciplinary and talented team. jpid78f3322jm jpit0834jm jpiy26jm

The Assistant Education Administrator develops and reviews policy for the establishment and operation of education, vocational, and leisure activity programs. Reviews policies from other disciplines for impact on education and recreation operations and provides feedback.

Evaluates existing programs, instructional methods, materials, and equipment to ensure a modern and responsive system of education and construction leisure activity programs.

Incumbent assists in the development and monitoring of an AOE budget of $5 to $6 million per year, the Reading is Fundamental and Artist-in-Residence budgets, and the Branch budget.

Provides leadership and coordinates efforts to establish standards for operational programs, monitors compliance with those standards and provides technical assistance in operations.
To be considered for the position, you must meet the following: Basic Requirements: A. Degree: that included or was supplemented by major study in education or in a subject-matter field appropriate to the position. OR B.

Combination of education and experience - courses equivalent to a major in education, or in a subject-matter field appropriate to the position, plus appropriate experience or additional course work that provided knowledge comparable to that normally acquired through the successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in A above.

AND In addition to meeting the above Basic Requirements, applicants must have: Education: There is no substitution of education for specialized experience for this position. Experience: At least one year of specialized experience equivalent in difficulty and complexity to the next lower grade level.

To be creditable, this experience must have equipped the applicant with the qualifications to perform successfully the duties of the position, and must typically be in or related to the position to be filled.

Some examples of this qualifying experience are: GS-13: - Experience assisting in the development of program quality standards. - Experience in designing and implementing data collection and reporting systems and research to assist in evaluating the effectiveness of education, vocational and leisure programs in the Federal Prisons System and facilitate positive inmate management. - Experience helping establish staffing standards in the selection of personnel to work in and supervise educational, vocational, and leisure-time programs within a correctional setting.

GS-14: - Experience developing and reviewing policy for the establishment and operation of education, vocational, and leisure activity programs. - Experience evaluating programs, instructional methods, materials, equipment, facilities and staff to ensure a current and responsive system of education, vocational and leisure activity programs. - Experience advising Program Review teams that review and evaluate inmate education, recreation, and training programs.

Credit will be given for paid and unpaid experience. To receive proper credit, you must show the actual time (such as the number of hours worked per week) spent in activities. **Your eligibility for consideration will be based on your responses to the questions in the application.**

Major Duties of the Position: The Associate Dean for Civics, Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences (CHASS): Provides academic leadership and portfolio administration (40%) for the CHASS academic portfolio, establishing priorities, translating senior-leader direction into executable academic objectives, and overseeing academic programs, curriculum, governance, assessment, scheduling, faculty utilization, resource requirements, and continuous improvement.

Ensures that CHASS operates as a coherent, integrated general-education program combining disciplinary rigor with intellectual breadth. Supervises and develops faculty and staff (25%), including civilian and military personnel and subordinate leaders as assigned.

Plans and assigns work; establishes performance expectations; evaluates performance; supports recruitment and staffing; identifies training and developmental needs; addresses employee concerns; and promotes organizational effectiveness, accountability, and a professional workplace.

Oversees curriculum integration, academic quality, assessment, and cadet development (20%) across the CHASS portfolio.

Guides curriculum development and review, academic standards, learning outcomes, instructional approaches, assessment, program evaluation, and interdisciplinary integration, ensuring that programs contribute effectively to cadets' development as critical thinkers, communicators, ethical decision-makers, and future officers.

Provides strategic integration, faculty development, and institutional engagement (15%) by developing faculty capability, encouraging scholarship and educational innovation, advising senior leaders on emerging academic and mission requirements, building partnerships, participating in institutional governance and strategic planning, and representing CHASS with USAFA, Department of the Air Force, academic institutions, government organizations, and professional and civic partners.

Advises senior academic leadership and manages portfolio resources, including personnel, workload, instructional support, technology, space, partnerships, and other mission requirements. Evaluates competing priorities, organizational risks, and resource implications and recommends appropriate courses of action.

May teach, mentor, advise, conduct scholarship or research, or participate in other academic activities when assigned and appropriately qualified; however, these duties support rather than replace the position's primary academic-administrative and supervisory responsibilities.
QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Applicants must be current USAFA faculty members and hold the academic rank of either associate professor (AD-1701-23) or Professor (AD-1701-24). USAFA faculty currently serving in an AD-1720-25 academic administration role with the requisite academic credentials are also eligible to apply.

ACADEMIC DISCIPLINES: Humanites, Arts, and Social Sciences.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS: We are particularly interested in senior faculty who bring: * A strong record as a USAFA educator. * Sustained superior performance in teaching, scholarship, and institutional service * Experience leading faculty, programs, courses, departments, or significant academic initiatives. * A record of teaching and scholarship in civics, humanities, arts, or social sciences that demonstrates intellectual breadth and serious interdisciplinary and/or integrated engagement. * A commitment to building a rigorous, formative, integrated general education program, with experience in common-core, primary-text, seminar, writing-intensive, Western civilization, civic education, or comparable undergraduate curricula and in developing disciplinary specialists as effective teachers within a common curriculum.

This position offers an unusual opportunity to help shape the intellectual architecture, faculty culture, and educational experience of a new School during its formative years. Inquiries about the position should be directed to the Search Committee Chair, Dr. Mark N. Jensen, mark.jensen@afacademy.af.edu.

Major Duties of the Position: The Associate Dean for STEM and Artificial Intelligence provides academic leadership and portfolio administration for the STEM and Artificial Intelligence academic portfolio, establishing priorities, translating senior-leader direction and emerging scientific and technological developments into executable academic objectives, and overseeing academic programs, curriculum, governance, assessment, laboratories and technical-learning environments, faculty utilization, resources, and continuous improvement.

Ensures the portfolio provides coherent, integrated technical general education rather than disconnected introductory specialist courses. Supervises and develops faculty and staff including civilian and military personnel and subordinate leaders as assigned.

Plans and assigns work; establishes performance expectations; evaluates performance; supports recruitment and staffing; identifies training and developmental needs; addresses employee concerns; and promotes organizational effectiveness, accountability, and a professional workplace.

Oversees curriculum integration, academic quality, assessment, and cadet technical development across the STEM and Artificial Intelligence portfolio.

Guides curriculum development, laboratories and hands-on learning, academic standards, assessment, and program improvement, with emphasis on scientific, quantitative, computational, systems, engineering, data, and technical judgment.

Ensures cadets develop the ability to reason from evidence, model and test solutions, evaluate uncertainty and tradeoffs, and address complex technical and national-security problems. Provides leadership for the responsible integration of artificial intelligence as a longitudinal capability within USAFA's technical general-education curriculum.

Ensures AI-enabled tools enhance rather than replace first-principles scientific, mathematical, computational, and engineering reasoning and that cadets develop appropriate understanding of validation, limitations, reliability, bias, human oversight, and responsibility for AI-informed decisions.

Provides strategic integration, faculty development, and institutional engagement by developing faculty and technical-educator capability, encouraging scholarship and educational innovation, advising senior leaders on emerging scientific and technological developments, and representing the portfolio with USAFA, Department of the Air Force, other service academies, universities, laboratories, government organizations, industry, and professional communities.

May teach, mentor, advise, conduct scholarship or research, or engage in engineering or other technical activities when assigned and appropriately qualified; however, these activities support rather than replace the position's primary academic-administrative and supervisory responsibilities.

The Associate Dean for STEM/AI is not expected to be an expert in every discipline or technology represented in the portfolio.

The position instead requires an academic leader capable of working among scientists, engineers, computing and AI specialists, and practitioners; asking good questions; identifying connections; protecting first-principles understanding; accelerating responsible adoption of emerging tools; and turning broad educational goals into a coherent and executable technical general-education program.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Doctoral degree Applicants must be current USAFA faculty members and hold the academic rank of either associate professor (AD-1701-23) or Professor (AD-1701-24). USAFA faculty currently serving in an AD-1720-25 academic administration role with the requisite academic credentials are also eligible to apply.

ACADEMIC DISCIPLINES: Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Artificial Intelligence, and related fields.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS: We are particularly interested in senior faculty who bring: a strong record as a USAFA educator; sustained superior performance in teaching, scholarship, and institutional service; experience leading faculty, programs, courses, departments, or significant academic initiatives; a record of teaching, scholarship, or professional activity in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, computing, artificial intelligence, or related fields that demonstrates interdisciplinary and/or integrated engagement; and a commitment to building rigorous, formative, integrated technical general education, with experience in hands-on or design-build-test education and demonstrated engagement with contemporary AI-enabled engineering or scientific practice; multidisciplinary professional experience in industry, government, national laboratories, military technical organizations, or comparable settings is highly valued.

This position offers an unusual opportunity to help shape the intellectual architecture, faculty culture, and educational experience of a new School during its formative years. Inquiries about the position should be directed to the Search Committee Chair, Dr. Mark Jensen, email: mark.jensen@afacademy.af.edu.

Major Duties of the Position: The Associate Dean for Warfighting Studies: - Provides academic leadership and portfolio administration (40%) for the Warfighting Studies academic portfolio, establishing priorities, translating senior-leader direction and emerging operational and technological developments into executable academic objectives, and overseeing curriculum, academic governance, assessment, faculty utilization, simulations, wargaming, experiential-learning environments, resources, and continuous improvement.

Ensures Warfighting Studies functions as a coherent developmental sequence rather than disconnected treatments of tactics, operations, and strategy. - Supervises and develops faculty and staff (25%), including civilian and military personnel and subordinate leaders as assigned.

Plans and assigns work; establishes performance expectations; evaluates performance; supports recruitment and staffing; identifies training and developmental needs; addresses employee concerns; and promotes accountability, professional development, and organizational effectiveness. - Oversees curriculum integration, academic quality, assessment, and cadet warfighting development (20%)across the portfolio.

Guides curriculum that connects tactical action to operational effects, campaigns, strategy, constitutional authority, political purpose, and national interest while developing a distinctive Airman and Guardian perspective integrated with joint, coalition, and multidomain operations. - Provides leadership for immersive and experiential warfighting education, including advanced wargaming, simulations, decision exercises, campaign analysis, planning activities, and digital operational environments.

Ensures these experiences require cadets to make consequential decisions against adaptive adversaries, assess outcomes, revise assumptions, and develop increasingly sophisticated judgment through repeated decision and after-action cycles. - Integrates emerging technology and the evolving character of war into the curriculum, including artificial intelligence, autonomy, cyber operations, contested space, sensing, electronic warfare, precision effects, and command and control, while maintaining attention to doctrine, human judgment, law, ethics, escalation, adversary adaptation, and political purpose. - Provides strategic integration, faculty and practitioner development, and institutional engagement (15%) by advising senior leaders, developing faculty and practitioner capability, encouraging scholarship and professional inquiry, and representing Warfighting Studies with USAFA, Department of the Air Force, other service academies, professional military education institutions, government organizations, universities, research centers, wargaming communities, industry, and other mission partners.

The Associate Dean for Warfighting Studies is not expected to be an expert in every service, domain, doctrine, technology, or operational specialty represented in the portfolio.

The position instead requires an academic leader capable of working with academics and practitioners from several fields; cultivating a distinctive Airman and Guardian perspective while remaining genuinely joint; understanding the emerging character of high-end conflict; asking good questions; identifying connections across domains and levels of war; making sound judgments; and turning broad educational goals into a coherent, immersive, and executable program.
QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Applicants must be current USAFA faculty members and hold the academic rank of either associate professor (AD-1701-23) or Professor (AD-1701-24). USAFA faculty currently serving in an AD-1720-25 academic administration role with the requisite academic credentials are also eligible to apply.

ACADEMIC DISCIPLINES: Relevant fields may include military, war, strategic, security, or national-security studies; military history; international relations; political science; defense policy; airpower; spacepower; cyber; AI; autonomous systems; electronic warfare; information operations; intelligence; operational planning or art; joint operations; wargaming; modeling and simulation; operations research; military innovation; defense technology; logistics; acquisition; professional military education; or another closely related field supporting Warfighting.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS: We are particularly interested in senior faculty who bring: - A strong record as a USAFA educator. - Sustained superior performance in teaching, scholarship, and institutional service. - Experience leading faculty, programs, courses, departments, military organizations, or significant academic initiatives. - A record of teaching, scholarship, or professional activity in military history, strategy, security studies, military operations, airpower, space power, cyber, joint or multidomain operations, or related fields that demonstrates interdisciplinary and/or integrated engagement with high-end warfighting problems. - A commitment to building a rigorous, formative, integrated warfighting program, with the ability to connect tactical, operational, and strategic problems across air, space, cyber, land, maritime, and undersea effects and experience with emerging technologies, advanced wargaming, simulation, digital operational environments, or comparable experiential learning strongly valued.

This position offers an unusual opportunity to help shape the intellectual architecture, faculty culture, and educational experience of a new School during its formative years. Inquiries about the position should be directed to the Search Committee Chair, Dr. Mark N. Jensen, email: mark.jensen@afacademy.af.edu.
